description: Durable verdict record authored exclusively by coordinator:spike at end-of-run — evidence that a mechanism was proven or disproven, not a baton. The contract deliberately defines no deployment_state/pickup_ready/status/claimed_by: this is not a handoff-shaped artifact and has no lifecycle to advance. (Their absence is a statement of the contract, not a rejection rule — like its sibling handoff schema this file leaves additionalProperties unset, so the guarantee here is definitional rather than enforced.) The one rule this schema does enforce structurally is the cross-field allOf below: it makes a verdict record with a live, unlanded routing intent UNWRITABLE — an author cannot record that a verdict gates something without also naming what took up that routing intent. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-07-28-spike-verdict-records-stable-evidence-home.md § C1

title.description: Human-readable label for the spiked mechanism.

created.description: Date the verdict record was authored (YYYY-MM-DD).

author.description: Session or agent identifier that authored this verdict record.

mechanism.description: What was spiked — the specific mechanism this record derisks or disproves.

verdict.description: CLOSED verdict enum. viable routes to coordinator:plan (or resumes a trampolined plan, per the plan⇄spike back-edge); not-viable routes back to shaping/re-derivation. No third value — an inconclusive spike is not a verdict record yet.

gated_route.description: REQUIRED key. Either a non-empty string naming what this verdict gates (the plan/decision/baton awaiting this mechanism to be proven or disproven), or the explicit literal null meaning this verdict gates nothing. An empty string is not a valid value for either state — use null. Cross-field rule below: a non-null, non-empty gated_route makes discharged_by required and non-null.

discharged_by.description: The plan/baton/commit/PM-facing surface that took up gated_route's routing intent. Nullable — null is only valid when gated_route is itself null (nothing to discharge). REQUIRED and non-null whenever gated_route is a non-empty string (enforced by the allOf cross-field rule below): a verdict record cannot assert a live routing intent without naming what took it up.

evidence_commit.description: Commit SHA carrying the empirical evidence for this verdict (spike scripts, probe output, measurements), or null when the evidence is captured entirely in this record's own prose.

allOf.description: The schema's real teeth: a non-null, non-empty gated_route makes discharged_by required and constrains it to a non-null, non-empty string — a verdict record with a live, unlanded routing intent is structurally unwritable. A null gated_route (this verdict gates nothing) does not trigger this rule; discharged_by is then free to be absent or null.
